text: Then came the strangest sultan of all, Muhammad bin Tughlaq, clever, well-read and full of big ideas.
In 1327, he decided to move the capital from Delhi to Dolatabad, about a thousand kilometers south,
and he ordered much of Delhi's population to move with him.

about the Sultanate years. Something new was also being made. Persian and Indian builders
mixed their styles in arches, domes and minarets. The poet Amir Khosrow wrote in a mix of Persian
and the local speech and is traditionally credited with shaping Kavali music.
Out of the bazaars and army camps, a whole new language grew. What would become Urdu
